name: Citizenship by Descent or Birth in Territory

requirements.blocker_text: Loi n° 35-1961 (Nationality Code), Articles 7 and 9: a child born to two Congolese parents is Congolese; a child with at least one Congolese parent (father OR mother) also qualifies, provided filiation is established -- explicitly gender-neutral on descent, and confirmed still gender-neutral in current practice per a CEDAW Committee note.
requirements.fix_path: Establish a parental link to a Congolese father or mother via a birth certificate.

requirement_groups.name: Born in Congo with a parent also born there

requirements.blocker_text: Article 8: a child born in Congo acquires nationality if either parent was also born in Congo, or if both parents are Congolese nationals born in the country.
requirements.fix_path: Establish birth in Congo together with a parent's own Congo birth (or both parents' Congolese nationality and Congo birth).

requirement_groups.name: Born in Congo to foreign parents, habitually resident since 16

requirements.blocker_text: Article 20: a person born in Congo to foreign parents acquires Congolese nationality upon reaching 21 years old, provided they are residing in Congo and have maintained habitual residence there since age 16.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain habitual residence in Congo from age 16 to 21 after being born there to foreign parents.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate showing parental link or place of birth
Proof of continuous habitual residence (majority-acquisition path only)

sources.title: Refworld -- Loi n° 35-1961 du 20 juin 1961 portant le Code de la nationalité congolaise: descent (Art. 7/9), birth-in-territory (Art. 8), majority acquisition (Art. 20)

Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- official gazette ('PARTIE OFFICIELLE') text of Loi n° 32-2011 modifying the 1961 Nationality Code: repeals the 7th paragraph of Art. 32, adds new Art. 47 on voluntary renunciation after acquiring a foreign nationality

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Republic of Congo / Congo-Brazzaville, ISO CG). STATUS: DRAFT -- both sources are tier 2 (intergovernmental/NGO-hosted primary legal text, not .gouv.cg government domains) by this dataset's own tiering rules, and the validator requires tier-1 sourcing for a hard requirement before a route can be published; this file is correctly modeled as draft from the outset rather than requiring a later correction (unlike Cameroon's equivalent files earlier in this session, which were initially mis-marked published and had to be downgraded). GENUINE, POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING: descent is explicitly gender-neutral ('father OR mother'), contrasting with Iraq's asymmetric Articles 3/4 found earlier in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true based on the 2015 Constitution's Article 19 ('all Congolese persons have the right to change nationality or to acquire a second one') and Loi 32-2011's voluntary-renunciation-only framework, corroborated by 2019 Canadian IRB research citing an honorary consul stating dual nationality has been permitted 'without any restrictions' since 2002 -- a clear, current-practice finding. GENUINE, DISCLOSED AMBIGUITY: Loi 32-2011 repeals the 7th paragraph of the old Article 32 without this build being able to confirm what that paragraph actually said (it may have been a renunciation requirement specifically for NATURALIZING foreigners, which would be a distinct question from whether BORN Congolese citizens can hold dual nationality) -- this dataset does not resolve that ambiguity by assumption.
